# Developer Bootstrap Script

The idempotent macOS setup script a developer runs to go from a fresh
machine to a running app. Every step checks its own state first, so it is
safe to run repeatedly. Usage, prerequisites and troubleshooting are in
[Developer Setup](dev-setup.md); this page is the script itself, reproduced
so it can be read without cloning the repository.

**The executable file is `scripts/bootstrap.sh` in the production build
repository, and this page is a copy of it.** A copy can drift, which is the
failure this handbook otherwise designs against, so the brain's test suite
compares the two whenever both are present: `npm test` runs
`scripts/test-bootstrap-sync.mjs`, which fails on any difference and skips
cleanly when the build repository is not cloned alongside this one. Change the
script and this page in the same unit of work.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#
# Scribl developer machine bootstrap, macOS.
#
# Idempotent by design: every step checks its own state first and skips when
# already satisfied, so running this repeatedly is safe and cheap. Nothing here
# uninstalls, downgrades, or overwrites a file you may have edited.
#
#   ./scripts/bootstrap.sh              install and configure what is missing
#   ./scripts/bootstrap.sh --check      report only, change nothing
#   ./scripts/bootstrap.sh --with-android   also set up the Android toolchain
#   ./scripts/bootstrap.sh --force-deps     reinstall npm dependencies
#
# What it deliberately does NOT do:
#   - Install Xcode. That is an App Store or Apple Developer download and needs
#     a human. The script detects it and tells you.
#   - Install Docker Desktop. It is commercially licensed above a published
#     org size and Bounteous is above it. Colima is installed instead.
#   - Touch any cloud account, deploy anything, or handle signing material.
#
# Written for bash 3.2, which is what macOS ships. No associative arrays, no
# mapfile, no ${var^^}. Keep it that way.
#
# See the Developer Setup page in the project brain's engineering handbook for
# the manual walkthrough and the reasoning.

set -uo pipefail

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

readonly REQUIRED_MACOS="14.5"
readonly REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR="22"
readonly REQUIRED_DISK_GB=100

readonly BREW_PACKAGES="fnm watchman cocoapods colima docker docker-compose awscli jq gh"

readonly MANAGED_PROFILE="$HOME/.scribl-dev.sh"
readonly MARKER_BEGIN="# >>> scribl dev setup >>>"
readonly MARKER_END="# <<< scribl dev setup <<<"

# Bitbucket, for the one sibling that did not move: scribl-app, the POC
# build repo (decision register 9.6). This repository's own remote,
# meta-scribl-app, moved to the client's GitHub org on 2026-09-02, so it is
# not in SIBLING_REPOS and is not cloned from REPO_HOST.
readonly REPO_HOST="git@bitbucket.org:hs2studio"
readonly SIBLING_REPOS="scribl-app"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

if [ -t 1 ]; then
  C_RESET=$'\033[0m'; C_BOLD=$'\033[1m'; C_DIM=$'\033[2m'
  C_RED=$'\033[31m'; C_GREEN=$'\033[32m'; C_YELLOW=$'\033[33m'; C_BLUE=$'\033[34m'
else
  C_RESET=''; C_BOLD=''; C_DIM=''; C_RED=''; C_GREEN=''; C_YELLOW=''; C_BLUE=''
fi

CHECK_ONLY=0
WITH_ANDROID=0
FORCE_DEPS=0

COUNT_DONE=0
COUNT_SKIP=0
COUNT_MANUAL=0
COUNT_WOULD=0
COUNT_FAIL=0
MANUAL_NOTES=""

# Every reporter returns 0 explicitly. These are used in `cmd && ok || fail`
# chains, where a reporter that returned non-zero would make BOTH branches run.
# Do not remove the `return 0` lines.
step()    { printf '\n%s==>%s %s%s%s\n' "$C_BLUE" "$C_RESET" "$C_BOLD" "$1" "$C_RESET"; return 0; }
ok()      { printf '  %s[ok]%s      %s\n' "$C_GREEN" "$C_RESET" "$1"; COUNT_DONE=$((COUNT_DONE + 1)); return 0; }
skip()    { printf '  %s[present]%s %s\n' "$C_DIM" "$C_RESET" "$1"; COUNT_SKIP=$((COUNT_SKIP + 1)); return 0; }
warn()    { printf '  %s[manual]%s  %s\n' "$C_YELLOW" "$C_RESET" "$1"; COUNT_MANUAL=$((COUNT_MANUAL + 1)); MANUAL_NOTES="${MANUAL_NOTES}  - $1\n"; return 0; }
fail()    { printf '  %s[fail]%s    %s\n' "$C_RED" "$C_RESET" "$1"; COUNT_FAIL=$((COUNT_FAIL + 1)); return 0; }
info()    { printf '  %s%s%s\n' "$C_DIM" "$1" "$C_RESET"; return 0; }
# `would` is a dry-run projection: something the script WOULD do. It is counted
# separately from `warn`, which is work only the developer can do. Conflating
# the two makes the --check summary lie about how much is left for a human.
would()   { printf '  %s[would]%s   %s\n' "$C_YELLOW" "$C_RESET" "$1"; COUNT_WOULD=$((COUNT_WOULD + 1)); }

die() { printf '\n%serror:%s %s\n\n' "$C_RED" "$C_RESET" "$1" >&2; exit 1; }

# Returns 0 when we are allowed to make changes.
acting() { [ "$CHECK_ONLY" -eq 0 ]; }

has() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Argument parsing
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

parse_args() {
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --check)         CHECK_ONLY=1 ;;
      --with-android)  WITH_ANDROID=1 ;;
      --force-deps)    FORCE_DEPS=1 ;;
      -h|--help)
        # Two plain substitutions rather than a BRE interval, which BSD and GNU
        # sed disagree about often enough to avoid entirely.
        sed -n '3,24p' "$0" | sed -e 's/^#$//' -e 's/^# //'
        exit 0
        ;;
      *) die "unknown argument: $1 (try --help)" ;;
    esac
    shift
  done
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Preflight
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Pure-bash dotted-version compare. Deliberately does NOT use `sort -V`:
# BSD sort on macOS is not a safe bet for that flag across OS versions, and a
# first-run script is the worst place to discover it. Compares field by field.
version_at_least() {
  local want="$1" have="$2"
  local want_rest="$want" have_rest="$have"
  local w h i

  # Bounded loop. Four fields is more than any macOS version needs.
  for i in 1 2 3 4; do
    w=${want_rest%%.*}
    h=${have_rest%%.*}

    # Strip non-digits so a suffix like "15.0-beta" cannot break arithmetic.
    w=$(printf '%s' "$w" | tr -cd '0-9')
    h=$(printf '%s' "$h" | tr -cd '0-9')
    [ -n "$w" ] || w=0
    [ -n "$h" ] || h=0

    [ "$h" -gt "$w" ] && return 0
    [ "$h" -lt "$w" ] && return 1

    case "$want_rest" in *.*) want_rest=${want_rest#*.} ;; *) want_rest=0 ;; esac
    case "$have_rest" in *.*) have_rest=${have_rest#*.} ;; *) have_rest=0 ;; esac
  done

  return 0
}

preflight() {
  step "Preflight"

  [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] || die "this script is macOS only"

  local os_version
  os_version=$(sw_vers -productVersion)
  if version_at_least "$REQUIRED_MACOS" "$os_version"; then
    skip "macOS $os_version"
  else
    die "macOS $REQUIRED_MACOS or newer required, found $os_version"
  fi

  local arch
  arch=$(uname -m)
  if [ "$arch" = "arm64" ]; then
    skip "Apple Silicon (arm64)"
  else
    warn "architecture is $arch, not arm64. If this is an Apple Silicon Mac you are in a Rosetta shell; open a native terminal and re-run"
  fi

  # -P forces single-line POSIX output so a long device name cannot wrap and
  # shift the columns. END rather than NR==2 for the same reason.
  local free_gb
  free_gb=$(df -Pg / 2>/dev/null | awk 'END {print $4}' | tr -cd '0-9')
  if [ -z "$free_gb" ]; then
    info "could not determine free disk space, continuing"
  elif [ "$free_gb" -ge "$REQUIRED_DISK_GB" ]; then
    skip "disk space ${free_gb}GB free"
  else
    warn "only ${free_gb}GB free, ${REQUIRED_DISK_GB}GB recommended. Xcode plus simulators plus dependencies will not fit comfortably"
  fi

  if [ "$CHECK_ONLY" -eq 1 ]; then
    info "running in --check mode, nothing will be changed"
  fi
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Xcode
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

setup_xcode() {
  step "Xcode and iOS platform"

  if [ ! -d /Applications/Xcode.app ]; then
    warn "Xcode is not installed. Install it from the App Store, then re-run this script. It is 10 to 15GB, so start it now and let it run"
    return
  fi
  skip "Xcode.app present"

  # Command line tools.
  if xcode-select -p >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    skip "command line tools installed"
  else
    if acting; then
      xcode-select --install 2>/dev/null || true
      warn "command line tools install started in a separate window. Finish it, then re-run"
      return
    else
      would "install command line tools"
    fi
  fi

  # Developer directory must point at full Xcode, not the CLT shim.
  local dev_dir
  dev_dir=$(xcode-select -p 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  case "$dev_dir" in
    /Applications/Xcode.app/*)
      skip "developer directory points at Xcode"
      ;;
    *)
      if acting; then
        info "switching developer directory to Xcode (needs sudo)"
        if sudo xcode-select --switch /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer; then
          ok "developer directory switched"
        else
          fail "could not switch developer directory"
        fi
      else
        would "switch developer directory from '$dev_dir' to Xcode"
      fi
      ;;
  esac

  # The license probe: xcodebuild fails until the license is accepted.
  if xcodebuild -version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    skip "Xcode license accepted ($(xcodebuild -version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1))"
  else
    if acting; then
      info "accepting Xcode license and running first launch (needs sudo)"
      sudo xcodebuild -license accept >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      if xcodebuild -version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ok "Xcode license accepted"
      else
        fail "Xcode still not usable. Open Xcode once manually and accept the prompts"
      fi
    else
      would "accept Xcode license and run first launch"
    fi
  fi

  # An iOS runtime has to exist or there are no simulators at all.
  if xcrun simctl list runtimes 2>/dev/null | grep -q "iOS"; then
    skip "iOS simulator runtime installed"
  else
    warn "no iOS simulator runtime. Open Xcode, Settings, Platforms, and install iOS. Recent Xcode does not bundle it"
  fi

  check_simulators
}

# The device floor is iPhone 11, phone first, iPad deferred out of this phase
# (decided 2026-08-26; Eric Rice, 2026-08-25 kickoff, 00:52:26 to 00:52:45).
# A developer needs two simulators, not whichever one Xcode created by default.
check_simulators() {
  local available
  available=$(xcrun simctl list devices available 2>/dev/null || echo "")

  if printf '%s' "$available" | grep -q "iPhone 11"; then
    skip "iPhone 11 simulator available (the device floor)"
  else
    warn "no iPhone 11 simulator. Create one in Xcode: it is the oldest supported device and the only honest place to judge canvas performance"
  fi
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Homebrew
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

brew_prefix() {
  if [ -x /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]; then echo /opt/homebrew
  elif [ -x /usr/local/bin/brew ]; then echo /usr/local
  else echo ""
  fi
}

setup_homebrew() {
  step "Homebrew"

  local prefix
  prefix=$(brew_prefix)

  if [ -n "$prefix" ]; then
    skip "Homebrew at $prefix"
  else
    if acting; then
      info "installing Homebrew, this will prompt for your password"
      if /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"; then
        prefix=$(brew_prefix)
        [ -n "$prefix" ] && ok "Homebrew installed at $prefix" || { fail "Homebrew install did not complete"; return 1; }
      else
        fail "Homebrew install failed"
        return 1
      fi
    else
      would "install Homebrew"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  # Make brew usable for the rest of this script run.
  eval "$("$prefix/bin/brew" shellenv)"
  return 0
}

setup_brew_packages() {
  step "Homebrew packages"

  if ! has brew; then
    warn "Homebrew unavailable, skipping packages"
    return
  fi

  # One listing, then match against it. Calling brew per package is slow.
  local installed pkg
  installed=$(brew list --formula -1 2>/dev/null || echo "")

  for pkg in $BREW_PACKAGES; do
    if printf '%s\n' "$installed" | grep -qx "$pkg"; then
      skip "$pkg"
    else
      if acting; then
        if brew install "$pkg" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          ok "$pkg installed"
        else
          fail "$pkg failed to install, run 'brew install $pkg' to see why"
        fi
      else
        would "install $pkg"
      fi
    fi
  done

  info "Docker Desktop is deliberately not installed: it is commercially licensed above a published org size. Colima provides a Docker-compatible runtime"
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Node
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

setup_node() {
  step "Node $REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR"

  if ! has fnm; then
    warn "fnm not available yet, skipping Node. Re-run after Homebrew packages install"
    return
  fi

  # fnm needs to be active in this shell to install or query versions.
  eval "$(fnm env --shell bash 2>/dev/null)" || true

  if fnm list 2>/dev/null | grep -q "v$REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR\."; then
    skip "Node $REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR installed"
  else
    if acting; then
      if fnm install "$REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ok "Node $REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR installed"
      else
        fail "could not install Node $REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR"
        return
      fi
    else
      would "install Node $REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR"
      return
    fi
  fi

  # Set the default unconditionally rather than parsing `fnm list` output,
  # whose format is not a stable contract. Setting the same default twice is
  # instant and harmless, which makes this the more idempotent option.
  if acting; then
    if fnm default "$REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      ok "Node $REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR is the default"
    else
      fail "could not set the default Node version"
    fi
  else
    would "ensure Node $REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR is the default"
  fi
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shell profile
#
# The managed file is rewritten wholesale every run, which makes it idempotent
# by construction. The user's own rc file only ever gains one guarded block,
# and only if that block is not already there, so repeated runs cannot stack
# duplicate exports. Nothing we did not write is ever modified.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

write_managed_profile() {
  local prefix shell_name
  prefix=$(brew_prefix)
  [ -n "$prefix" ] || prefix="/opt/homebrew"

  # Resolve the shell name here, at write time, and bake it in literally.
  # Expanding ${SHELL##*/} inside the generated file would evaluate it in the
  # user's shell at every startup, where SHELL may be unset or unexpected.
  shell_name=$(current_shell_name)

  cat > "$MANAGED_PROFILE" <<EOF
# Managed by scribl-mobile-app/scripts/bootstrap.sh
# This file is REWRITTEN on every bootstrap run. Do not edit it.
# Put your own customisations in your shell rc file instead.

# Homebrew
[ -x "$prefix/bin/brew" ] && eval "\$($prefix/bin/brew shellenv)"

# Node version manager, switches on directory change via .node-version
command -v fnm >/dev/null 2>&1 && eval "\$(fnm env --use-on-cd --shell $shell_name)"

# Android, only meaningful once the SDK is installed
if [ -d "\$HOME/Library/Android/sdk" ]; then
  export ANDROID_HOME="\$HOME/Library/Android/sdk"
  export PATH="\$PATH:\$ANDROID_HOME/emulator:\$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools"
fi
EOF
}

# SHELL is guarded because `set -u` makes an unset variable fatal, and a login
# shell spawned oddly (some CI and remote sessions) may not export it. zsh is
# the macOS default, so it is the right fallback.
current_shell_name() {
  local s="${SHELL:-/bin/zsh}"
  case "${s##*/}" in
    zsh)  echo "zsh" ;;
    bash) echo "bash" ;;
    *)    echo "zsh" ;;
  esac
}

rc_file_for_shell() {
  case "$(current_shell_name)" in
    bash) echo "$HOME/.bash_profile" ;;
    *)    echo "$HOME/.zshrc" ;;
  esac
}

setup_shell_profile() {
  step "Shell profile"

  local rc
  rc=$(rc_file_for_shell)

  if acting; then
    write_managed_profile
    ok "wrote $MANAGED_PROFILE"
  else
    would "write $MANAGED_PROFILE"
  fi

  if [ -f "$rc" ] && grep -qF "$MARKER_BEGIN" "$rc"; then
    skip "$rc already sources the managed profile"
    return
  fi

  if acting; then
    {
      printf '\n%s\n' "$MARKER_BEGIN"
      printf '[ -f "%s" ] && . "%s"\n' "$MANAGED_PROFILE" "$MANAGED_PROFILE"
      printf '%s\n' "$MARKER_END"
    } >> "$rc"
    ok "added the managed block to $rc"
    info "open a new terminal, or run: . $MANAGED_PROFILE"
  else
    would "add a source line to $rc"
  fi
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Container runtime
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

setup_colima() {
  step "Container runtime"

  if ! has colima; then
    warn "colima not installed yet, skipping. Re-run after Homebrew packages install"
    return
  fi

  if colima status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    skip "Colima is running"
  else
    if acting; then
      info "starting Colima, first start provisions a VM and takes a minute"
      # Sizing flags only apply when creating the VM. If one already exists
      # with different specs, passing them can be rejected (a disk cannot
      # shrink), so fall back to starting the existing VM as it is.
      if colima start --cpu 4 --memory 8 --disk 60 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ok "Colima started"
      elif colima start >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ok "Colima started with its existing configuration"
        info "the VM predates this script, so its cpu, memory and disk are whatever it was created with"
      else
        fail "Colima failed to start, run 'colima start' to see why"
        return
      fi
    else
      would "start Colima"
      return
    fi
  fi

  if docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ok "Docker socket reachable"
  else
    fail "Docker socket not reachable even though Colima is up. Try 'colima restart'"
  fi

  info "Colima does not auto-start on login. Run 'colima start' after a reboot, or add it to your login items"
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Git and repositories
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

setup_git_identity() {
  step "Git identity"

  local name email
  name=$(git config --global user.name 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  email=$(git config --global user.email 2>/dev/null || echo "")

  # Explicit if/else rather than `test && skip || warn`, which runs BOTH
  # branches if the middle command ever returns non-zero.
  if [ -n "$name" ]; then
    skip "user.name is '$name'"
  else
    warn "git user.name is unset: git config --global user.name 'Your Name'"
  fi

  if [ -n "$email" ]; then
    skip "user.email is '$email'"
  else
    warn "git user.email is unset: git config --global user.email 'you@bounteous.com'"
  fi

  # Only set conventions the team agreed, and only when unset.
  set_git_default pull.rebase true
  set_git_default init.defaultBranch main
}

set_git_default() {
  local key="$1" value="$2" current
  current=$(git config --global "$key" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ -n "$current" ]; then
    skip "$key is '$current'"
  elif acting; then
    git config --global "$key" "$value" && ok "$key set to $value"
  else
    would "set $key to $value"
  fi
}

bitbucket_reachable() {
  # BatchMode stops a first-time host-key prompt from hanging the script, and
  # the timeout stops a silent network stall from doing the same. Probed
  # against scribl-app, the one sibling still on Bitbucket (decision register
  # 9.6): this repo's own remote and meta-scribl-app's are both GitHub now, so
  # neither is a Bitbucket-reachability signal.
  GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o ConnectTimeout=10" \
    git ls-remote --exit-code "$REPO_HOST/scribl-app.git" HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1
}

github_reachable() {
  # No specific repo to probe here: the client's GitHub org name is not
  # recorded yet (see dev-setup.md section 7), so this checks auth against
  # the host generically rather than a repository that may not exist in this
  # script's view.
  GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o ConnectTimeout=10" \
    ssh -T git@github.com >/dev/null 2>&1
  # GitHub's SSH auth check exits 1 on a successful, authenticated connection
  # and only fails to connect at all on a real problem, so treat exit 255
  # (unreachable or rejected) as the failure and anything else as reachable.
  [ "$?" -ne 255 ]
}

setup_repos() {
  step "Sibling repositories"

  local root repo
  root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
  info "workspace root: $root"

  if ! bitbucket_reachable; then
    warn "cannot reach Bitbucket over SSH. Add your key (ssh-keygen -t ed25519, then paste ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub into Bitbucket). If the key is already there, you probably need adding to the HS2 Studio workspace: a repo invitation alone is not enough"
    return
  fi
  skip "Bitbucket reachable over SSH"

  if ! github_reachable; then
    warn "cannot reach GitHub over SSH. This repository's own remote is on the client's GitHub org (decision register 9.6); add your key there too, and confirm on the team channel who is requesting your org invite"
  else
    skip "GitHub reachable over SSH"
  fi

  # Plain clones. The brain used to vendor the app repo as a git submodule and
  # no longer does, so there is nothing to initialise and no pin to advance.
  for repo in $SIBLING_REPOS; do
    if [ -d "$root/$repo/.git" ]; then
      skip "$repo cloned"
    else
      if acting; then
        info "cloning $repo"
        if git clone "$REPO_HOST/$repo.git" "$root/$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          ok "$repo cloned"
        else
          fail "could not clone $repo"
        fi
      else
        would "clone $repo into $root"
      fi
    fi
  done
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project dependencies
#
# The scaffold may not have run yet, so every step here degrades to a note
# rather than an error when the file it needs does not exist.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

setup_env_file() {
  step "Environment file"

  local repo
  repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)

  if [ ! -f "$repo/.env.example" ]; then
    info ".env.example does not exist yet, the scaffold has not created it. Nothing to do"
    return
  fi

  if [ -f "$repo/.env" ]; then
    skip ".env exists, leaving it alone"
    return
  fi

  if acting; then
    cp "$repo/.env.example" "$repo/.env" && ok ".env created from .env.example"
    info "review .env before running the app. DATABASE_URL must point at localhost"
  else
    would "create .env from .env.example"
  fi
}

install_npm_deps() {
  local dir="$1" label="$2"

  if [ ! -f "$dir/package.json" ]; then
    info "$label has no package.json yet, skipping"
    return
  fi

  if [ -d "$dir/node_modules" ] && [ "$FORCE_DEPS" -eq 0 ]; then
    skip "$label dependencies installed (--force-deps to reinstall)"
    return
  fi

  if acting; then
    info "installing $label dependencies, this takes a while"
    if (cd "$dir" && npm install >/dev/null 2>&1); then
      ok "$label dependencies installed"
    else
      fail "$label npm install failed, run it directly to see the error"
    fi
  else
    would "install $label dependencies"
  fi
}

setup_project_deps() {
  step "Project dependencies"

  if ! has node; then
    warn "node not on PATH in this shell. Open a new terminal and re-run"
    return
  fi

  local node_major
  node_major=$(node --version | sed 's/^v\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  if [ "$node_major" = "$REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR" ]; then
    skip "node $(node --version)"
  else
    warn "node $(node --version) is active but $REQUIRED_NODE_MAJOR is required. Open a new terminal so fnm can switch"
  fi

  local repo
  repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
  install_npm_deps "$repo" "app"
  install_npm_deps "$repo/backend" "backend"
}

setup_playwright() {
  step "Playwright browsers"

  local repo
  repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)

  if [ ! -d "$repo/node_modules/@playwright" ]; then
    info "Playwright is not a dependency yet, skipping"
    return
  fi

  if [ -d "$HOME/Library/Caches/ms-playwright" ]; then
    skip "Playwright browsers cached"
    return
  fi

  if acting; then
    (cd "$repo" && npx playwright install chromium >/dev/null 2>&1) \
      && ok "Chromium installed for Playwright" \
      || fail "Playwright browser install failed"
  else
    would "install Chromium for Playwright"
  fi
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Android, opt in
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

setup_android() {
  step "Android toolchain"

  if [ "$WITH_ANDROID" -eq 0 ]; then
    info "skipped, pass --with-android to set it up. Android is a fast follow, so this is optional today"
    return
  fi

  if ! has brew; then
    warn "Homebrew unavailable, skipping Android"
    return
  fi

  local casks cask
  casks=$(brew list --cask -1 2>/dev/null || echo "")

  for cask in temurin@17 android-studio; do
    if printf '%s\n' "$casks" | grep -qx "$cask"; then
      skip "$cask"
    elif acting; then
      brew install --cask "$cask" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
        && ok "$cask installed" \
        || fail "$cask failed to install"
    else
      would "install $cask"
    fi
  done

  if [ -d "$HOME/Library/Android/sdk" ]; then
    skip "Android SDK present"
  else
    warn "Android SDK not installed. Open Android Studio, run the setup wizard, and install an SDK plus an emulator image. The managed profile already exports ANDROID_HOME once it exists"
  fi
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Summary
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

summary() {
  printf '\n%s%s%s\n' "$C_BOLD" "----------------------------------------------------------------" "$C_RESET"
  printf '%sSummary%s  ' "$C_BOLD" "$C_RESET"

  if [ "$CHECK_ONLY" -eq 1 ]; then
    printf '%s%d would change%s  %s%d already present%s  %s%d need you%s  %s%d failed%s\n' \
      "$C_YELLOW" "$COUNT_WOULD" "$C_RESET" \
      "$C_DIM" "$COUNT_SKIP" "$C_RESET" \
      "$C_YELLOW" "$COUNT_MANUAL" "$C_RESET" \
      "$C_RED" "$COUNT_FAIL" "$C_RESET"
  else
    printf '%s%d changed%s  %s%d already present%s  %s%d need you%s  %s%d failed%s\n' \
      "$C_GREEN" "$COUNT_DONE" "$C_RESET" \
      "$C_DIM" "$COUNT_SKIP" "$C_RESET" \
      "$C_YELLOW" "$COUNT_MANUAL" "$C_RESET" \
      "$C_RED" "$COUNT_FAIL" "$C_RESET"
  fi

  if [ -n "$MANUAL_NOTES" ]; then
    printf '\n%sThings only you can do:%s\n' "$C_BOLD" "$C_RESET"
    printf '%b' "$MANUAL_NOTES"
  fi

  printf '\n%sNext:%s\n' "$C_BOLD" "$C_RESET"
  if [ "$CHECK_ONLY" -eq 1 ]; then
    printf '  1. Nothing was changed. Re-run without --check to apply the items above.\n'
    printf '  2. Install Xcode first if it is listed, since it is the long download.\n'
  else
    printf '  1. Open a new terminal so the shell profile takes effect.\n'
    printf '  2. Re-run this script. It is idempotent, and it will confirm what is now satisfied.\n'
    printf '  3. Once the scaffold has landed: npm run dev, then npx expo run:ios.\n'
  fi
  printf '\n  Manual walkthrough and troubleshooting: the Developer Setup page\n'
  printf '  in the project brain, handbook/engineering/dev-setup.md\n'
  printf '  Blocked on something external: QUESTIONS.md\n\n'

  [ "$COUNT_FAIL" -eq 0 ] || return 1
  return 0
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

main() {
  parse_args "$@"

  printf '%s%s%s\n' "$C_BOLD" "Scribl developer bootstrap" "$C_RESET"
  printf '%sIdempotent: safe to run as many times as you like.%s\n' "$C_DIM" "$C_RESET"

  preflight
  setup_homebrew
  setup_brew_packages
  setup_node
  setup_shell_profile
  setup_xcode
  setup_colima
  setup_git_identity
  setup_repos
  setup_env_file
  setup_project_deps
  setup_playwright
  setup_android

  summary
}

main "$@"
```
